scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole (AITA) in this situation. Let me break it down step by step. First, the background: I'm Jewish, and I'm 26. My dad is 55, introverted and quiet, very intelligent but not great at executing ideas. I'm more impulsive and get things done, like my granddad. I took my dad's business idea, got IP rights, and started a business two years ago. It's been a massive success, into six figures, with potential for millions in the next five years. When I took the idea, my dad was upset but didn't say much. My mom was proud. I confronted him, and he called me a "fucking asshole," feeling betrayed. My sister defended him, but my mom and granddad support me. I offered him 20% of profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I think he's being unreasonable because I took his idea and made it successful, but he's upset. I understand his feelings but think he's not seeing the bigger picture. Now, considering AITA: Did I do something wrong? Let's see. 1. **Ownership of the Idea**: My dad came up with the idea. I took it without his consent. Even if he wasn't going to execute it, is it right to take it as your own? 2. **Execution vs. Ideas**: My dad is good at ideas but not execution. I'm the opposite. So, I took his idea and executed it successfully. But does that mean I own it? 3. **Ethics of Taking the Idea**: Is it stealing? Legally, if I got IP rights without his knowledge, that's a problem. But if I just took the idea and didn't involve him, is that stealing? 4. **Emotional Impact**: My dad felt betrayed. Even if I think he's being unreasonable, his feelings are valid. Betrayal is a strong emotion, especially from a child. 5. **Offering Profit Share**: I offered him 20%, which is generous, but he refused. Maybe he feels that the idea's value is more than 20%, or he's hurt and can't accept it. 6. **Family Dynamics**: My mom and granddad support me, but my dad and sister are against me. This could create long-term family tension. 7. **Moral Perspective**: Is it wrong to take someone's idea and profit from it without giving them proper credit or share? Even if they couldn't execute it, the idea is theirs. 8. **Alternative Actions**: Could I have approached my dad differently? Maybe discussed the idea with him, offered partnership, or at least acknowledged his contribution publicly. 9. **Consequences**: The business is successful, but at the cost of a strained relationship with my dad. Is that a fair trade-off? 10. **Personal Growth**: Have I considered how this action reflects on me? Am I being respectful and fair, or am I prioritizing success over relationships? In summary, while I made the business successful, I may have overlooked the emotional and ethical aspects of taking my dad's idea without his consent. Offering a profit share was a good gesture, but it doesn't fully address the betrayal he felt. It's possible that I'm being an asshole because I didn't consider his feelings and the ownership of his idea.
